paragraphs.text: (With Christ, 26 May 1974)
Isaiah 53: 10, 11 (first clause); Psalm 133: 1–3

No doubt, beloved brethren, these scriptures have often been used. One’s thought in regard to them is the pleasure of God, which I think is a matter for us to consider, and especially that it is in such good hands, “The pleasure of Jehovah shall prosper in his hand”. How establishing it is just to have a sense of that, over against all the enemy’s efforts to disrupt and intrude and spoil; how encouraging that the prophet could say that “the pleasure of Jehovah shall prosper in his hand”. We can have some sense of how much is bound up in this, “The pleasure of Jehovah”.

It also says, “Yet it pleased Jehovah to bruise him”. It is very affecting that it should be put that way. So much is bound up in these words. It pleased Jehovah to bruise Him, that this result might be brought about. “He hath subjected him to suffering”—we cannot say much about that; we can just bow worshipfully as we contemplate it. It is very blessed to contemplate that there is going to be an answer to the suffering. There is a seed, “He shall see a seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of Jehovah shall prosper in his hand”.
I find great encouragement in that, beloved brethren, and in linking it with Psalm 133 which says, “How good and how pleasant it is for brethren

to dwell together in unity!”. I think, first of all, that the pleasure would be for God, although, of course, it is very blessed to experience something of this—brethren dwelling together in unity. It is very pleasant for us to experience that, very blessed to have a sense of it, but then to think of what there is for God in it. It does not say how many brethren. I think that is a great encouragement in these days. In some localities there are very, very few, but dwelling together in unity is possible. And it is for the pleasure of God, Jehovah’s pleasure is in it.

Then it goes on, “For there hath Jehovah commanded the blessing, life for evermore”. That again is very comforting and establishing; that God has commanded a blessing. It does not wholly depend on us, although it might in a sense, but in this aspect of it, it is God’s doing, God commands the blessing. It is God’s delight to have saints in the enjoyment of life, life for evermore. This is a subject that has been much before us in these past days, the enjoyment of eternal life. How encouraging it is to read that God has commanded it, God has commanded the blessing. How stimulating it is, and how encouraged one feels for oneself, just to answer to the promptings of the Holy Spirit in the ministry. Luke speaks of “walking and praising God” (Acts 3: 9), that is what God has in mind for every one of us.

So as we think of the many young people in the localities represented here today how encouraging it is just to think of Jehovah’s pleasure bound up in His people. “The pleasure of Jehovah shall prosper in his hand”, and God is commanding the blessing. It should stimulate and encourage us to have greater zeal and committal to walk so as to please God, thinking always of the Lord Jesus in

His distinctiveness. He could say that He always did the things that pleased the Father (John 8: 29). He was the only One of whom that could be said, “For the Christ also did not please himself”, Romans 15: 3. Much of our time is connected with pleasing ourselves; we would have humbly to acknowledge that, but let us think of One who was here and who pleased not Himself; His sole concern was the pleasure of Jehovah. May we be stimulated, beloved brethren, on this line, for His name’s sake.
P. van den Berg
Genesis 24: 58–67; Colossians 1: 12–15; Revelation 22: 16, 17

I think the Lord would help us, dear brethren, in considering these passages in view of our being transferred into the realm where divine love is operating. There is great need for being transferred if the Lord is moving in view of leading the saints into the inheritance, and what is in the divine mind for us. I think it is a great thing that there might be readiness on our part to move according to divine speaking so that we might come into the best that God has for us. It is a great thing to lay hold of the calling of God, what we have been called into, what our portion is with Christ on the other side of death, and that we submit ourselves to the service of the blessed Holy Spirit who is here to guide us into all the truth. It is wonderful what God has prepared for those who love Him, “Things which eye has not seen, and ear not heard, and which have not come into man’s heart, which God has prepared for them that love him, but God has revealed to us by his Spirit”, 1 Corinthians 2: 9, 10. We often stop at that one verse, but we want to go on to the other—“but God has revealed to us by his Spirit; for the Spirit searches all things, even the depths of God”. So it is a great thing to “go with this man”, a great matter to follow the blessed Holy Spirit in what He would lead us into.

“For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sans of God”, Romans 8: 14—God has in view that we should enter into the inheritance, that we should enter into His purpose, that we should not remain in the wilderness but enter into our proper place, an inheritance amongst the sanctified. He desires that we should lay hold of life eternal, that we should see His purpose expressed in Christ and lay hold of it, and that we should thus rise to the height of the heavenly calling, seeing what our place is in sonship in the presence of the Father and answering to it, that we might be brought into the liberty of sonship. The Spirit would help us to get into the liberty of sonship. “Ye have not received a spirit of bondage again for fear ... but a spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father”, Romans 8: 15. That is what is due to God, and He desires an answer in the light of it because sonship is for God. We are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus and He has given us the Holy Spirit so that we might be conscious of it, conscious of our relationship, and that we might respond to God because the Father has delivered us from the authority of darkness. He has brought us out of Egypt in view of our serving Him, “Let my son go, that he may serve me”, Exodus 4: 23. What a thing that is, that we serve God and that we serve Him not in a spirit of bondage, but as persons who are affected by divine grace. We have been set free from the authority of darkness, set free from so many things that the enemy would use to detain us, to hold us, things that are of the earth, things in our circumstances, things in family life, that detain us.

Dear brethren, I think we could all do more in being available for God that we might serve Him. It has great recompense because grace operating in the land results in there being more in the way of prosperity amongst the saints. We would all desire the prosperity of the saints in every locality represented here. It says prophetically that the pleasure of Jehovah prospers in the hand of Jesus (Isaiah 53: 10). How wonderful that is! The Father has committed all things in the hand of the Son and things are prospering in His hand, but how important it is that we should be under the hand of Christ, that we should be marked by heavenly desires. That is open to the youngest amongst us. It was seen in the family of Caleb and in the family of Joshua, who were persons who had an appreciation of the heavenly inheritance. Joshua says, “As for me and my house, we will serve Jehovah” (Joshua 24: 15), and Caleb has a daughter who has right desires. She has desires for the upper springs and the nether springs (see Judges 1: 15). She has desires for the things of God and God gives us according to our desires. He wants to attract us into all that His love has prepared for us because the land is a very, very good land, a land flowing with milk and honey, a land flowing with heavenly blessings. There is nothing that can fill our hearts in the scene in which we are, but think of what God has prepared for those that love Him and how the Spirit would help us to enjoy the wealth of it. It is all prepared for us in Christ, for Christ is the expression of the purpose of God.

So sonship is for God, but eternal life is for us. Eternal life is the blessing that God gives to persons—what is “really life”. Paul says to Timothy, “Lay hold of eternal life”, 1 Timothy 6: 12. It is in the inheritance. It is in the enjoyment of our heavenly relations with divine Persons and with one another, in the company of the saints, as loving them. At occasions like this we experience something of eternal life as we enjoy our relations with one another, engaged with heavenly things in an out-of-the-world condition. You are not thinking of the shops outside and the things out there. You just leave it for the moment and enjoy what is in an out-of-the-world condition of things altogether where Christ is your portion.

So although we are in wilderness conditions (and the leading of the Spirit is largely in the wilderness), the Spirit would engage us with a Man in another world. Whatever our circumstances may be in the wilderness we would be ready for transfer, because in taking up our daily responsibilities we would be conscious that our life is not there, but is bound up with the saints in another world—“Our commonwealth has its existence in the heavens, from which also we await the Lord Jesus Christ as Saviour, who shall transform our body of humiliation into conformity to his body of glory”, Philippians 3: 20, 21.

Dear brethren, the coming of the Lord Jesus is very near, it is imminent. Things in the world are worsening, but things among the saints should be getting better and better. It says, “Let the filthy make himself filthy still ... and he that is holy, let him be sanctified still”, Revelation 22: 11. It is either the one way or the other. It is either deterioration or it is going in for what is best, and God has reserved what is best for the end, “Better is the end of a thing than its beginning”, Ecclesiastes 7: 8. I think the end of the dispensation will be real blessing. Psalm 133 shows how the oil flows down from the head of Aaron right down to the hem of his garments, and I believe that is just where we are. We are at the end of the dispensation, and there is a peculiar testimony as a result of it; nothing great in the world, but something that is known amongst the saints, known to persons who discern the Lord’s movements in the sanctuary, hearing the bells as the High Priest moves into the sanctuary; it is something that has come down by the Holy Spirit to the hem of Aaron’s garments. The hem is the finish and I think God is just looking for the finish. He is looking for what is complete, even in a day of breakdown. We want to wake up to the fact that God is arriving at what is complete, what is according to the pattern; that in a day of small things the seven lamps are still there and God has not given up His thoughts in spite of the scattering there has been.

If you read the book of Zechariah you see there had been a scattering, but God came in to counteract it. There was a young man, and Jerusalem was measured, the breadth and the length of it, and God says, I have yet chosen Jerusalem; I have not given up my thoughts in relation to the assembly. A young man, no doubt Zechariah himself, wakes up and sees the seven lamps. I want the young brethren and all of us—including oneself—to wake up to the fact that the assembly is the assembly and the seven lamps are there, and that the house is being built by the hands of Zerubbabel and that he will finish it. There will be the shoutings, “Grace, grace unto it!” when the headstone is brought forth. It says, “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, saith Jehovah of hosts”, Zechariah 4: 6, 7. So we have the Holy Spirit here and it is an authoritative voice; and yet it is a question of love and readiness to “go with this man”, whether we are prepared to be taken where the Holy Spirit would have us, whether we are prepared to go in for what He is presenting to us in relation to another Man.

The Spirit has in view that the assembly should be for Christ, that in every locality there should be an answer for Him in the light of what is so precious to His heart. He loved the assembly and delivered Himself up for it, and as you think of the assembly today you would value what is available in the light of it in persons, in localities, where things are worked out according to the pattern, where the saints are in touch with the living voice of the Holy Spirit as it comes to us in the ministry that the Lord is giving, because that is an evidence of where the Lord is. It is a great matter to go in for all that God has prepared for those that love Him and His thoughts will never change. Whatever there may have been in the way of breakdown, God is not defeated—He has everything in His own hands.

In John 21 the Lord had everything ready. In spite of all that was going on the Lord did not interfere and He did not go on the sea. He did not come in in that way at all. He just stands there with everything ready for them and says, “Children, have ye anything to eat?” (John 21: 5). It is a question of what there is for Christ. Well, dear brethren, how are we in our hearts in relation to Christ? Will we go in for what the Holy Spirit would present to us in relation to that Man? In John 4 the Lord is just available in that position at the well when that woman came and she was really brought to one Man. She had had many husbands, but the Lord touched her affections. He touched her in her history and she came to it that nothing was hidden in the sight of the One with whom she had to do, that He knew all about her. She said, “I see that thou art a prophet”, and then the Lord is able to say, “Woman”. The Lord was able to say that because she discerned the prophetic voice and so, in principle, the assembly comes to light and the Lord is able to bring her in her thoughts into the very highest features of the service of God. Then she goes into the city. She leaves her water-pot. She is ready, set free by the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus from the law of sin and of death, and she goes into the city and says, “Come, see a man”. A Man—she had another Man before her! Well, that is enough for us, dear brethren; that is what the Holy Spirit is presenting to us. That is what Paul was labouring for that he might present the Corinthians to one Man, not to two different objects, one Object, the good part that Mary had chosen in Luke 10 that was not going to be taken from her.

So it is a question of one Man. We have been delivered from “the authority of darkness, and translated into the kingdom of the Son of his love”. I think it is a great matter in Colossians to be ready to cross Jordan, to find that there is a Man on the other side of death. Christ at the right hand of God, and that our minds are set in relation to the things above, not on the things that are on the earth. There is so much that is not exactly worldly. We have to be very careful, dear brethren, in not allowing worldly things. But the enemy would also deprive us of the enjoyment of our heavenly part by drawing us into earthly things, things that are really against the cross of Christ. You will remember that Paul speaks to the Philippians, even weeping, of some who are “enemies of the cross of Christ ... who mind earthly things”, Philippians 3: 18, 19. They only talk about earthly things to you, and when you speak about heavenly things they are silent, you have no point of contact with them. Well, brethren, “Our commonwealth has its existence in the heavens”! The word ‘commonwealth’ involves the way that we share common interests and are able to talk about them. “Then they that feared Jehovah spoke often one to another”, Malachi 3: 16. They were not waiting for things here, they were waiting for the Sun of righteousness to appear. Heaven was very attentive, and took notice of what was there.

What a sight it must have been to heaven in the beginning of Luke—Simeon, Anna, and others, the shepherds in the field—how interested heaven was in them. There was no visitation of Jerusalem, except to Zacharias, and there was unbelief with him, but there were those who were in the divine current and they would be engaged with these things as Mary want into the hill country—and what godly conversation there was! I think that searches us all as to where our interests are. Where our treasure is, there also is our heart (Matthew 6: 21). We have been transferred into “the kingdom of the Son of his love”. O, dear brethren, what a thing it is to be transferred, to make a moral journey, because the ministry has that in mind in view of every man being presented perfect in Christ; that we should arrive at the heavenly Man, “at the measure of the stature of the fulness of the Christ” (Ephesians 4: 13), that we might arrive at the knowledge of the Son of God, at the full-grown man, that we should not be babes, or dwarfs. Oh what need there is for increase, that we may increase in the things of God, that there may be a growing up amongst us, that we may grow in grace and in the knowledge of God.

So at the end the Lord Jesus is presenting Himself to the assemblies. The prophetic line is going on to completion and there is an answer at the end of the dispensation. There is what is ready to be transferred. You find in Enoch’s life a picture of the way things will move on to completion. When the point came that Enoch was translated, there was not much of a change. For Enoch it was not a big change when the Lord took him, because he was right there. He walked with God, and I think it tests us all as to how much we are with God in matters. There are things in the testimony that come, and will come, and will be a test to us. The Lord has helped us to see the pattern. He has helped us to see how things are in the divine mind, and that things are to be worked out according to the pattern, that we are to be governed by divine principles, and that whatever feelings we might have in a natural way they are not to be given any place in anything that occurs amongst the saints. The question is where the Lord is in any matter, and that tests us as to how much we are with God. It is a question of being with God, a question of priesthood, a question of right feelings. Things are to be according to God and we are to consider for what is due to God in the light of His assembly before we allow any other consideration to enter into the matter. Then you will find that something in the character of the bride, the Lamb’s wife, will come to light, faithfulness assembly-wise to the One who suffered here in maintaining the truth, in maintaining the testimony.

Standing before Pilate He witnessed the good confession. When Pilate said, “Thou art then a king?” the Lord answered, “I have been born for this, and for this I have come into the world, that I might bear witness to the truth”, John 18: 37. The Lord suffered rather than surrender the truth in the face of the enemy, and there is an answer to that in the assembly, the bride, the Lamb’s wife. She comes through in this passage. Jesus presenting Himself as “the root and offspring of David, the bright and morning star”. What a presentation it is! We are tested as we read the promise of the Lord to the overcomer at Philadelphia, “I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God ... and my new name”, Revelation 3: 12. I trust, dear brethren, we have got a little further in our understanding of the light that God has given us as brought out in the ministry of the recovery. I believe there is something in the new name that has come out in ministry, and as we proceed the Lord presents Himself here as “the root and offspring of David”, “the root” referring to His deity and “the offspring” to His manhood. He came in in Matthew according to the line of David, but then He was David’s Lord. He was before David; He was the root of David. He is also “the bright and morning star”—that alludes to the prophetic line of ministry that goes through until the Lord Jesus comes, as Peter speaks of it, “We have the prophetic word made surer ... (as … a lamp shining in an obscure place) until the day dawn and the morning star arise in your hearts”, 2 Peter 1: 19.

Well, I wonder, dear brethren, how much Christ is in the ascendancy in each of our hearts, because He is the bright and morning star and He wants a greater place in our affections, in all our hearts. And the Holy Spirit would rejoice and delight in any greater apprehension and appreciation of Christ on our part, and particularly in bridal features in the recognition of Him as Head of the assembly, the glorious Person who will see things through for His own delight and glory and for the delight and pleasure of God. The pleasure of Jehovah prospers in the hand of Christ. He has been entrusted with all that the Father has. It says that, after Rebecca was brought to Isaac, “Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac”, Genesis 25; 5. Well, God has given all things to be in the hand of Christ. How worthy He is, beloved brethren! It says that God has “granted him a name, that which is above every name”, Philippians 2: 9. It does not say what that name is, but He has given Him a name that is above every name. May the Lord help us that our hearts and our affections may be set in relation to Christ, that there may be more committal on our part to Himself and to His interests here, and that the Spirit may have His way with each one of us, for His name’s sake.

articles.title: ALL BLESSING IS IN COMPANY WITH CHRIST
articles.author: W. C. Lock

paragraphs.text: I want to speak about the thought of the Christ, about Jesus, and about the Son of God. When we are thinking of Christ, we think about the One who has done so much for God and so much for man. When we are thinking about Jesus, we think of the One who subdues us all into serviceability, “ourselves your bondman for Jesus’ sake”, 2 Corinthians 4: 5. He is also the One who helps us to leave the earth—“his life is taken from the earth”. But if our life is taken from the earth, Paul immediately says, ‘Yes, but here is the Son of God and another sphere’. That is, you do not need to live in relation to the things on the earth now; Jesus has died to deliver us from all this scene of things where there is so much travail and sorrow, and there is another world of which the Head and Centre is God’s Son. That is, I think, where we would like to get everybody to enjoy Christ, where He is now. That is really the full gospel, enjoying Christ where He is—the Man in glory!

But, you know, we are in a very perilous scene and Samaria pretty well corresponds; that is, there are certain religious trimmings to the world. The churches are at every street corner pretty near, like the Samaritans. The woman of John 4 says, “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. There is a lot of that! But the real question is. Have we a link with God? Have we really found what Christ has done for God and for men? Christ is the anointed One, the One singled out to resolve these terrible matters of sins and sin—I say it in that order—and the bondage of the enemy. This city was in bondage. They had this man Simon who claimed to be something (Well, we have known something of that too), and Peter said to him, “Thy money go with thee to destruction” (Acts 8: 20). How often the enemy seeks to introduce another man to detract from what God is doing.

But Philip goes down and announces the glad tidings of the word. That is one thing, it is the word of God; we should always remember that. “And Philip, going down to a city of Samaria, preached the Christ to them; and the crowds with one accord gave heed to the things spoken by Philip, when they heard him and saw the signs which he wrought”. When it is a question of the anointing, there is power. We must think of that—when you come into the presence of one who has the Spirit, there is power. Those who came into the presence of Christ, suddenly became conscious of wonderful power there, and virtue. That woman in Matthew 9 said “If I should only touch his garment”. There was virtue! She knew there was healing there.

If you say, ‘I would like to be able to leave these things that hold me in bondage’, well, I think the thought of the Christ will help you. There is power, power in view of that situation being met. It is very affecting that God has come into the scene of the enemy’s power and broken it. God in Christ came into this very scene of suffering, came into this city of Samaria, and spoiled the enemy’s goods in the centre of his operations. And He has come into my heart, where the enemy was so firmly entrenched. He displaced the enemy and installed another Man there. That is what God can do. He can come into the scene of the enemy’s activities and displace him, but He does not leave it empty.

One of the worst things that I see in relation to the preaching of the gospel is that certain persons get a verse of Scripture and say, ‘Yes, my sins are forgiven’, and then for years and years they go on living to themselves without thinking of Christ, of God, or of the Spirit of God. It is like the house, you know, unoccupied, swept, and adorned and then it says seven worse spirits came (Matthew 12: 44, 45), and that often happens. If you have started to move towards the Lord Jesus do not be content until your heart is filled. The great thing in christianity is to be filled. It is very interesting in John 2 you get, “Fill the water vessels”, and then in John 6, it says that, “when they had been filled”. Jesus said, “Gather together the fragments”. There is nothing worse than a christian who is not filled. He is not enjoying this world, and he is not enjoying God’s world. You just deprive yourself of all the gain that the Spirit has in mind to introduce us into. Peter quotes in Acts 4: 25, 26, “Why have the nations raged haughtily and the peoples meditated vain things? The kings of the earth were there, and the rulers

were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ”. The enemy knows that, Christ having come in, his power is more than met, that he is spoiled. One of the greatest enemies that the testimony ever had was Saul of Tarsus and God made him the greatest trophy of grace. He spoiled the enemy’s camp and secured the opposer as His own servant— an elect vessel!

Now what God is after is vessels, and vessels have to be filled. The great point in the preaching of the word is, I believe, that the vessels become filled. I know myself that often my heart is not as full as it should be. But the christian’s heart should be full, whether it is in appreciation of Christ in manhood or of the thoughts of God, or of the Spirit having come. I connect the idea of the patience of God with the Spirit. The Spirit has been here nearly two thousand years and in all our afflictions He was afflicted. Think of what the Spirit has felt about all the catastrophies that have come in. But then, maybe, the enemy is intruding into my affections today. That is the point to get through to, that the enemy might be intruding himself and displacing Christ in my heart! Ezekiel 14: 4 refers to every man setting up his idols in his heart. My idol might not be yours, and yours might not be mine. Unless we are careful, unless Christ is in my heart, there is always something that is going to intrude to mar and spoil the joy. It says here, “There was great joy in that city”. There is joy as the result of the preaching of the word. What is in mind in christianity is that sad people become happy, poor people become rich, and people who are unattractive become beautiful. It changes everything around, and what is in mind in the preaching is that persons become changed around as well. Paul refers to himself as having been an insolent overbearing man, but he became a meek

and gentle man and could thus speak of “my ways as they are in Christ”, 1 Corinthians 4: 17. Now Philip is going down to the desert. He had a great big audience in Samaria but now he is going to one man. God is interested in the ones—Thank God that He is! I was not sitting in the preaching when I was converted. I was out on the prairie by myself and God spoke to me. God has His own ways of speaking, but He can get through to you and He can tell you about Himself and He can tell you about yourself—He did both!

The eunuch was reading the Scriptures. It shows that even if you do not understand them (this man did not), you should still read them. There is nothing like the Scriptures to help you to understand something of the God you have. He had been worshipping at Jerusalem, but he did not know the Lord. He was reading the prophet Esaias, “And the Spirit said to Philip, Approach and join this chariot. And Philip, running up, heard him reading the prophet Esaias, and said, Dost thou then know what thou art reading of? And he said. How should I then be able unless some one guide me?”. Well, thank God, you might not know what you are reading if you read the Scriptures, but there are those who can guide you and help you, and the Spirit is here to guide and help you. “And he begged Philip to come up and sit with him. And the passage of the scripture which he read was this: He was led as a sheep to slaughter, and as a lamb is dumb in presence of him that shears him, thus he opened not his mouth”. It is wonderful to think of the Lord Jesus in those final hours! He did not call down judgment; He did not condemn the people who nailed Him to the cross. He did not rail at the Jews and the priests. When He was reviled, He reviled not again. Peter tells us. “He opens not his mouth”—when He

did open His mouth it was to pray for people—“Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do”, Luke 23: 34. It is very affecting that in Luke 24: 47 the Lord says, “That repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all the nations beginning at Jerusalem”. The very place where He was crucified was the very place where the gospel was first proclaimed and that is where I see this dispensation of grace. Thus Paul, the greatest enemy, who persecuted, murdered, and dragged to prison—women and children included— became a trophy of divine grace. And that grace is not limited to Paul. You may have been far off; you may not be too far on even now, but you can be a trophy of divine grace, so that men can take account of the fact that you are not just saved but that God has enriched you with the knowledge of Himself in Christ.

“In his humiliation his judgment has been taken away”. The Lord did not defend Himself. Never! Was it a right judgment when they condemned Him to death? It was not! I think of this verse, “in his humiliation his judgment was taken away”, at the Supper every Lord’s day, because we really reverse the unjust judgment of men. We say, ‘He is worthy—He died, but He is worthy to live’. There was no right judgment in relation to the way the Lord was condemned. Pilate said, “I find no fault whatever in him”, John 18: 38. They could not find anything of which to accuse Him. They even got false witnesses and the witnesses did not agree. Pilate said, “I have found no cause of death in him” (Luke 23: 22), but they still crucified Him. Pilate just sent Him away to Herod and there was not one who could find a single reason to put Him to death. But He went on to the cross and to death; not that there was anything in Him worthy of death; it was because of our sins that He was nailed to the tree.
So He “bore our sins in his body on the tree”, 1 Peter 2: 24.

We cannot say that He bore the sins of all; a most important matter this, because we got into trouble on that seven or eight years ago. It was said that He bore the sins of all. It is not true—Mr. Raven was very, very clear as to that. If you say to a man on the street that Christ has borne his sins, well, what is the need for conversion? You have got to tell him that he has to face up to, and adjust, the matter and realise his need of a Saviour. The sacrifice is for all— He “gave himself a ransom for all” (1 Timothy 2: 6), but can you say He bore your sins? We have in 1 Corinthians 15: 3, “Christ died for our sins, according to the scriptures; and that he was buried; and that he was raised the third day, according to the scriptures”. Our sins—is there anybody here who is not just sure that their sins have been borne by the Lord Jesus on Calvary’s tree? I tell you there is nothing like the feeling when you know those sins have gone for ever, the gladness of it! The enemy, Satan, is the great accuser. He accused Luther, saying you did this and you did that, and Luther told him to write across the list of charges, “The blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanses us from all sin”, 1 John 1: 7. It is a wonderful thing that the vilest sinner can be forgiven. The Lord says, “All sins shall be forgiven” (Mark 3: 28), except, of course, speaking injuriously against the Holy Spirit. But all manner, a murderer, a thief, and anyone else you want to name, can get clear as accepting the perfect offering of Christ as having met the righteous claims of God as to sin. This is an individual matter, “Repent ... each one of you ... Be saved from this perverse generation”, Acts 2: 38– 40.

Then it says here, “His life is taken from the earth”. People say, ‘Well, I know I have to leave the world because of Christ’. Yes, but in Philippians 3: 19 Paul refers to earthly things those “who mind earthly things”, and I think that is something we are going to have to be careful about. We would not go into systems of men, we would not go to picture shows, for instance, or to football games, or other such things, but earthly things sometimes creep in. It may be reading, it might be pictures, or whatever it might be, but earthly things. Those who mind earthly things lose the joy that the eunuch found. “His life is taken from the earth”, not just from the world. He gave Himself for us “so that he should deliver us out of the present evil world” (Galatians 1: 4), but let us also watch that we are clear of earthly things.

Then it says, “And Philip, opening his mouth and beginning from that scripture, announced the glad tidings of Jesus to him”—of Jesus. What a Person is presented in the gospel! Not only the One who is officially the Christ, that is one thing, but now we are coming to the personal side. The book of the Revelation makes so much of the name of Jesus, as if at the very end that is what the Spirit of God would project upon our affections. “I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify these things to you in the assemblies”, Revelation 22: 16. That is, it is not just the One who has officially taken up every matter for God and secured them in righteousness, but it is the One who would affect our hearts. How the name of Jesus affected the apostle! He says in 2 Corinthians 4: 10, “Always bearing about in the body the dying of Jesus, that the life also of Jesus may be manifested in our body”. That is why we are left here, that there might be a testimony to the Man whose life is taken from the earth. Somebody went to Teignmouth, where Mr. Coates lived, and asked

where he lived and the boy that he asked said, ‘Oh, you mean the man who looks like Jesus’. You see, there was a testimony. It was not official, it was just the impression the boy had. Mr. Coates left that impression—one who was like Jesus. I think, “For Jesus’ sake”, is a wonderful leverage in the soul. It is like what we were saying yesterday, that we might please Him who has enlisted us as soldiers (2 Timothy 2: 4). So we need to think of the testimony of Jesus and the glad tidings of Jesus because it was that which affected this man.

When he gets to this point then the next word is as to water and baptism. The eunuch was not baptised as a baby, but if the life of Jesus was taken from the earth, then, he says, ‘Here is water—If He has gone this way, there is only one righteous thing for me to do—to go the same way’. That is answering to your baptism, you see. Your parents baptised you, rightly; now your conviction—and mine—is that we have to answer to it; that is, if this is the way that Jesus went, then I am going that way too. And that is how I am going to be happy, as it says, the eunuch went on his way rejoicing. That is fine! You know, it is as we leave this world that we begin to be happy. People do not think it, but that is the truth as you come out of the world and live in relation to another world of which the centre is God’s Son.

Now I just want to say a word about that because the Son of God brings in the idea of another world and new associations. It is not that God is just relieving me of the burden of my sins— that is very, very wonderful, but the thought of God’s Son is that He is the centre of another world and He wants me to be there too; He wants you to be there. God’s Son is alive in heaven today. Right now that Man is in the glory. He is there in manhood—a

real man! I know who He is as to His Person; do not get me wrong. I know who that Person is, but a Man is in heaven, a Man is in glory and a Man has been glorified! But God is not satisfied with having that only. Because of the greatness of what Christ has done God is bringing many sons to glory too, in association with Christ. You must remember that all the blessings in christianity are in relation to Christ, as it says in Romans 8: 32, “He who, yea, has not spared his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not also with him grant us all things”—with Him. All the blessings in christianity come in company with Christ. That is Colossians; you have to be with Him where He is. “Seek the things which are above, where the Christ is” (Colossians 3: 1). The point in christianity is that God has wonderful thoughts but they are all expressed in Christ, not only as a Man down here walking His lowly pathway, but rather in the One who is glorified as having effected atonement, redemption, justification, reconciliation, and numerous other things, and the One as to whom it says, “God has sent out the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father”, Galatians 4: 6. I wonder whether there is anybody here who has never been consciously brought to that point—not just saying Abba, Father, because the Spirit of God in the Scriptures does not say ‘whereby we say, Abba, Father’; whether it is in Romans or Galatians the word is, ‘crying Abba, Father’, as if there is a certain intensity in the appreciation of the great thoughts of God that would glorify us in association with Christ. He can glorify us because Christ is glorified.

It is a marvellous thing that Christ is glorified and the great fact now is that God in bringing many sons to glory has made perfect the Leader of their salvation through sufferings (Hebrews 2: 10). It is a marvellous gospel that we can leave this scene of trial and tribulation and sadness—and do not let us minimize that—and that we can have wonderful joy, and the heart be filled, as we realise that Christ is on high and the Spirit is here to attach us to Him where He is. May God bless this word and may our hearts find greater place for that One whom we know as Jesus, for His name’s sake.

“THE ANCIENT PATHS” Jehovah appeals to His erring people in Jeremiah 6: 16, “Ask for the ancient paths, which is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls”. Have any of us left the ancient paths—perhaps brought up in the truth, but having wandered from it? The ancient paths remain. The gospel in all its glory and divine completion remains; the light of it is shining in the face of Jesus. The teaching and fellowship of the apostles remains (Acts 2: 42), and all that Paul ministered remains, to be enjoyed and answered to. The present word of the Lord, and the voice of the Spirit, would call upon us to ask for the ancient paths, the good way, and to walk therein. Thus shall we find rest.
